title: Modeling the impact of acute cannabis consumption on pupil light response using nested-crossed function-on-scalar regression
content:
Summary
The widespread legalization of cannabis has created an urgent need for objective measures of recent use that are robust to tolerance effects, particularly among frequent users. Curves of pupil response to light stimuli, analyzed using functional data methods, offer a promising avenue. We analyze pupil response curves collected via handheld pupillometers, from both eyes at 3 time points for daily, occasional, and noncannabis users. To model these data, we develop a novel function-on-scalar regression framework that accounts for within- and across-curve correlation arising from the repeated and nested structure of the observations. Our approach uses method-of-moments estimators to estimate covariance matrices for nested-crossed functional random effects, enabling computationally efficient inference for fixed effects. Results reveal significant differences in pupil light response between cannabis users and nonusers that persist up to 100 min post-use, demonstrating the potential of pupillometers for detecting recent cannabis use in roadside and workplace settings.
